idiom_name: none - throwing prototype stubs plus JSDoc @interface / @implements (documentation only)
implementation_notes: JavaScript deliberately has no contract construct, and a class that only declares one resolves to methods that throw Error('not implemented'): the failure arrives at the first call, and only for the members actually called, while instanceof-style checks test provenance rather than capability and reject structurally valid objects (literals, proxies, objects from another realm). The idiomatic answer is the language's own structural model: name the operations the caller needs, document the shape with JSDoc (@typedef / @interface plus @implements) and let a checker enforce it - // @ts-check in the file, or TypeScript at the boundary - with a small runtime shape assertion only where untrusted objects cross a plugin boundary. Keep a nominal base class only when implementations must also share default behaviour, which is a different decision from declaring a stateless contract.
pitfalls: A stub method fails only when it is called, so an incomplete implementation can pass review and fail on one code path; an up-front shape assertion at the boundary turns that into a startup error.

instanceof and other nominal checks reject correct structural implementations, including object literals and objects created in another realm or worker: the check answers where the object was made, not what it can do.
JSDoc and // @ts-check protect only the files that opt in, and an untyped caller can still pass any object, so nothing enforces the documented contract where checking is absent.
alternative: Structural contracts instead of a contract class: document the required shape with JSDoc (@typedef or @interface plus @implements) and enforce it statically with // @ts-check or by moving the boundary to TypeScript; add a small runtime shape check (every required member is a function) where untrusted objects cross a plugin or configuration boundary. Use an abstract base class only when implementations must also share default behaviour.
